matt-ops: Heads up — we rolled the CUDA 12.2 rebuilt containers to a subset of us-west GPU nodes ~10m ago and now seeing runtime loader/linker failures, processes get SIGABRT or segfault immediately after libcuda load.
laura-sre: any repeatable log sample? which image tag did we push?
sam-runtime: image tag is inference/cuda12-rebuild:2026-03-17b. Getting this on ~12 nodes:
```
ERROR: symbol lookup error: /opt/cuda/lib64/libnccl.so.2: undefined symbol: ncclCommInitRank
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
priyanka-ml: hitting this on P4 and A10 nodes? or just A100s?
matt-ops: mostly A10s in us-west-2a and 2c. A100 nodes show different failure: 
```
/opt/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11: version `CUDA_12.0' not found (required by ./bin/infer)
```
laura-sre: sounds like the container runtime expects CUDA 12 user libs but host driver / libcuda is older or ABI mismatched. Did we also upgrade drivers on those nodes?
deploy-bot: deploy event: inference/cuda12-rebuild:2026-03-17b -> us-west GPU pool (canary 10%)
kernel-ops: we did not touch drivers today. Nodes are on NVIDIA driver 510.xx (for CUDA 11). That mismatch would explain missing CUDA_12 symbols.
sam-runtime: but these containers were rebuilt from base with compiled wheels against CUDA 12 toolkits — they include libcudart 12.x in-image which still expects a compatible kernel driver/libcuda on host. Looks like we accidentally mixed a CUDA12 userland with CUDA11 driver.
priyanka-ml: observed NCCL ops stall for some jobs — hang at allreduce with no network errors, metrics show processes alive but stuck in ncclCommInit.
laura-sre: action plan proposals: (1) revert canary to previous image (cuda11-compatible) immediately, (2) schedule driver upgrade on a subset with maintenance window and test, (3) add node-level preflight check for libcuda/GLIBC/CUDA symbols before allowing image with newer userland. Thoughts?
matt-ops: +1 on revert. Reverting now to inference/cuda11-stable:2026-02-10 across canary. Will patch rollout and watch.
oncall-bot: Revert initiated by matt-ops at 2026-03-17T16:05Z. Rolling restart of canary nodes started.
kernel-ops: long-term fix: either bundle libcuda stub in the container (risky for performance and driver functionality) or avoid shipping userland compiled for newer CUDA without driver check. Prefer upgrade drivers cluster-side after validation.
sam-runtime: we should also update our image admission controller: fail images whose CUDA ABI version > host kernel driver reported via /proc/driver/nvidia/version on nodes used in canary. Prevents this mismatch.
priyanka-ml: can we add a runtime sanity test to CI that launches a tiny NCCL job across 2 vhosts using the built image to catch this? probably cheap and would catch linker symbol mismatches.
laura-sre: agree. Also need to review cost/availability impact: driver upgrades need node reboots and reserved capacity could be affected. Estimate for us-west GPU pool: ~3h maintenance and ~2% capacity loss during rolling.
matt-ops: revert completed on canary; initial reports look clean. I'll hold on broader rollout until driver plan is agreed.
oncall-bot: Incident note: LD/ABI mismatch detected, revert applied to canary.
kernel-ops: one oddball: a node with modular driver install had /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1. Wrong symlink pointed to older version despite driver package being updated last month. We should audit symlinks as part of driver prep.
laura-sre: can someone open a small postmortem with timeline and checklist for next upgrade? include who signs off on driver vs userland changes.
sam-runtime: I'll draft the checklist: driver compatibility matrix per model binary, admission controller rule, CI ncck sanity job, and rollback playbook.
priyanka-ml: FYI some customers running heavy embedding pipelines might have seen elevated latency during canary revert. We should flag support.
matt-ops: noted — pinged support to prepare notes. Thanks all.
laura-sre: thanks — marking this thread for follow-up items and owner assignments.
